inbox.title: Capture
inbox.body: Drop a word, phrase, grammar doubt, or writing idea in seconds — no need to decide where it belongs yet. Add an optional note or source, keep items in To process, then turn a capture into Vocabulary, Theory, Writing, or Exercise when you have time. An item is marked Processed only after you finish creating that linked entry.

vocabulary.title: Vocabulary
vocabulary.body: Add your own words and phrases with meanings, example sentences, pronunciation, and tags. Organize by topic, level, or situation — then reuse them in exercises and review. Start with words from daily life, lessons, books, or media; your library becomes the foundation for practice.

theory.title: Theory
theory.body: Save grammar rules, pronunciation notes, usage explanations, and personal examples in your own words. Think of Theory as a reference notebook you return to whenever you forget something. The more you document, the stronger your personal knowledge base grows.

exercises.title: Exercise
exercises.body: Practice with flashcards, quizzes, fill-in-the-blank, and more — built from your own vocabulary and theory. Exercises grow with the knowledge you add. The more material you save, the more useful and personalized your practice becomes.

writing.title: Writing
writing.body: Draft texts and create question sets using your own topics and vocabulary. Writing is for actively using what you learn, not just memorizing it. With Pro, AI can check and improve your work, and you can export materials when needed.

listening.title: Listening
listening.body: Upload audio or video, get a transcript, and turn it into a lesson. Use the transcript to catch unfamiliar words and expressions, then practice with real content you choose. Bring your own listening materials instead of being limited to predefined content.

speaking.title: Speaking
speaking.body: Call an AI tutor on video and practice speaking naturally with your own learning knowledge. After each session, review the transcript and feedback to see what to improve. This closes the loop: learn → practice → use → review → improve.

addWord.title: 1. Add a word
addWord.body: Start building your personal vocabulary. Add words and phrases you actually want to remember — then fill in meanings, examples, and tags on the next screen.

search.title: 2. Search your library
search.body: Search your vocabulary instead of scrolling through everything. Try a word, meaning, or tag.

filters.title: 3. Filter and organize
filters.body: Narrow by part of speech, tags, or sort order. Use tags to group words by topic, level, or situation.

library.title: 4. Your word library
library.body: Your saved words live here. Open any entry to edit it, or use them in exercises and review later.

vocabularyAdd.title: Add a word
vocabularyAdd.description: This form is the heart of Notoria — each field helps you remember and reuse the word later.

word.title: 1. Type the word
word.body: Enter the word or phrase you’re learning. This becomes the main entry in your vocabulary bank.

partOfSpeech.title: 2. Part of speech
partOfSpeech.body: Choose noun, verb, adjective, and so on. It helps filters and AI suggestions stay accurate.

meanings.title: 3. Meanings
meanings.body: Add one or more meanings. Star up to 5 primary meanings for exercises — others stay for reference. Drag to reorder.

examples.title: 4. Example sentences
examples.body: Add sentences that show how the word is used. Open Additional details for a translation or note if you need one.

tags.title: 5. Tags
tags.body: Tag by level, topic, or situation so you can find and practice related words later.

synonyms.title: 6. Synonyms
synonyms.body: Link related words from your bank to connect entries and deepen recall.

notes.title: 7. Notes
notes.body: Optional free-form notes — pronunciation tips, usage quirks, or anything you want to remember.

save.title: 8. Save
save.body: When you’re ready, save the word. You can edit it anytime from your vocabulary library.

writing.title: Writing
writing.description: Use what you've learned in your own sentences — drafts, question sets, and pieces you can revisit.

create.title: 1. Start writing
create.body: Create a text or writing exercise based on something you want to practice. Your writing doesn't need to be perfect — use it to experiment and notice what you still need to learn.

search.title: 2. Search
search.body: Find a piece quickly by title or content instead of browsing everything manually.

filters.title: 3. Filter
filters.body: Narrow by level, topic, formality, or sort order to organize your writing library.

library.title: 4. Your writing library
library.body: Open a piece to keep writing. With Pro, you can also use AI to check and improve your work, or export when you need a copy.

newFolder.title: 5. Create a folder
newFolder.body: Click New folder to group writing by topic, level, or project. Folders are optional — you can keep everything at the top level too.

nameFolder.title: 6. Name your folder
nameFolder.body: Type a name that helps you find things later (for example Essay drafts or B1 worksheets). The folder is created inside the location you are viewing.

organize.title: 7. Folders and files
organize.body: Folders sit above your writing list. Open a folder to work inside it — new pieces you create there are saved in that folder automatically.

moveItem.title: 8. Move between folders
moveItem.body: Use the move icon on any piece, or drag it onto a folder card. You can also drag folders into other folders to nest topics.

theory.title: Theory
theory.description: Keep the explanations you want to remember — grammar, pronunciation, usage, and personal notes.

add.title: 1. Add a note
add.body: Create a theory note for something you want to remember. When you write it, pick a category so related topics stay together.

category.title: 2. Browse by category
category.body: Filter notes by category to jump back to grammar, pronunciation, usage, or other topics you've saved.

search.title: 3. Search
search.body: Search your theory library to find a note quickly instead of hunting through everything.

read.title: 4. Read and revisit
read.body: Open a note whenever you need a refresher. Come back as often as you like — this is your reference notebook.

newFolder.title: 5. Create a folder
newFolder.body: Click New folder to group theory notes by topic, unit, or exam. Folders are optional — your notes can stay at the top level too.

nameFolder.title: 6. Name your folder
nameFolder.body: Type a clear name (for example Grammar B1 or Pronunciation). The folder is created inside the location you are viewing.

organize.title: 7. Folders and files
organize.body: Folders appear above your notes. Open a folder to see only what is inside — new notes you create there are saved in that folder.

moveItem.title: 8. Move notes between folders
moveItem.body: Use the move icon on any note, or drag it onto a folder. You can also nest folders inside each other to organize by topic.

exercise.title: Exercises
exercise.description: Turn your knowledge into practice — flashcards, quizzes, fill-in-the-blank, and more.

sources.title: 1. Choose your source
sources.body: Practice from vocabulary you've saved, theory notes, or imported material. The more you add, the more useful your practice becomes.

types.title: 2. Pick an exercise type
types.body: Choose flashcards, multiple choice, match pairs, fill in the blank, type the answer, or form a sentence — then start a short session with your own knowledge.

listening.title: Listening
listening.description: Bring real content you want to understand — upload audio or video, read the transcript, and study from it.

upload.title: 1. Upload your material
upload.body: Bring something you actually want to understand — a podcast, video, lesson, or your own recording.

uploadArea.title: 2. Choose a file
uploadArea.body: Select or drop an audio or video file. Notoria will upload it and generate a transcript where supported.

lessons.title: 3. Study your lessons
lessons.body: Open a lesson to read the transcript, catch new words and expressions, and practice with the material you chose.

newFolder.title: 4. Create a folder
newFolder.body: Click New folder to group lessons by topic, course, or skill level. Folders are optional — you can keep everything at the top level.

nameFolder.title: 5. Name your folder
nameFolder.body: Type a name that makes sense to you (for example Podcasts or Exam prep). The folder is created inside the location you are viewing.

organize.title: 6. Folders and files
organize.body: Folders appear above your lessons. Open a folder to browse only that group — uploads you add while inside a folder are saved there.

moveItem.title: 7. Move lessons between folders
moveItem.body: Use the move icon on any lesson, or drag it onto a folder card. You can also nest folders to organize larger collections.

speaking.title: Speaking
speaking.description: Practice using the language in conversation — then review the transcript and feedback.

start.title: 1. Start a session
start.body: Create a speaking session and join when you're ready. Practice using the language in a real conversation instead of only studying it.

sessions.title: 2. Review afterward
sessions.body: Open a session to read the transcript and feedback. Use it to spot mistakes, reuse useful phrases, and decide what to add to your diary next.

inbox.title: Capture
inbox.description: Save scraps fast — words, doubts, ideas — then turn them into real study items when you have a moment.

capture.title: 1. Capture something
capture.body: Use Capture to save a word, phrase, grammar doubt, or writing idea without deciding where it belongs yet. Speed matters more than perfect structure here.

filters.title: 2. To process vs processed
filters.body: To process holds items still waiting. Processed shows captures you already turned into vocabulary, theory, writing, or exercises.

search.title: 3. Search
search.body: Filter the current tab by content, note, or source so you can find a capture quickly.

sort.title: 4. Sort
sort.body: Sort by newest, oldest, or name so the list matches how you want to work through it.

list.title: 5. Your capture list
list.body: Each card shows the content, optional note/source, and when you saved it. Open the ··· menu on a card to process it.

process.title: 6. Process into Notoria
process.body: Send a capture to Vocabulary, Theory, Writing, or Exercise. It only becomes Processed after you finish saving there — canceling the create form leaves it waiting.

meta.title: Welcome to Notoria
meta.description: Everything you need to know about building your personal language-learning diary and turning your knowledge into practice.

welcome.title: What is Notoria?
welcome.lead: Notoria is your private learning diary.
paragraphs: Think of it as a notebook for your language journey — except everything you write down can become part of your practice.
There is no predefined curriculum you have to follow. There is no "correct" way to use your workspace. There is no teacher watching over your shoulder. Nobody is grading your notes.
welcome.examplesIntro: You decide what belongs in your Notoria. For example, you can:
examples: Write down a word you heard today
Save a grammar rule you finally understood
Add an example sentence that makes sense to you
Upload a video you want to study
Write about something you want to practice saying
welcome.overTime: Over time, these small pieces become your own personal language knowledge base.

noWrongWay.title: There is no right or wrong way to build your diary.
paragraphs: Your learning diary is yours. You don't have to organize everything perfectly. You don't have to use every feature. You don't have to follow a particular learning method.
Use Notoria in whatever way makes learning easier and more meaningful to you. The goal is not to create a perfect database — the goal is to create a learning space that actually belongs to you.

howItWorks.title: How Notoria works
howItWorks.intro: Notoria connects your learning areas into one journey:
howItWorks.anywhereNote: You can start anywhere, but many people follow a path like this:

collect.title: 1. Collect your knowledge
collect.body: Use Capture for quick scraps, then add vocabulary and theory from lessons, conversations, books, media, or anywhere you meet the language.

understand.title: 2. Understand it
understand.body: Keep your own explanations, examples, grammar notes, and pronunciation notes — written in a way that makes sense to you.

practice.title: 3. Practice it
practice.body: Turn what you've collected into exercises built from your own words and knowledge.

use.title: 4. Use it
use.body: Practice writing, listening, and speaking with the language you've been building.

review.title: 5. Review it
review.body: Look back at what you struggled with, add what you learned, and keep growing your diary.

howItWorks.connectedNote: These areas work together — not as separate apps. What you add in Vocabulary and Theory feeds your exercises, writing, listening, and speaking.

vocabulary.title: Vocabulary
vocabulary.intro: Vocabulary is your personal word library — the foundation of everything else in Notoria.
bullets: Add words and phrases you actually encounter
Include meanings, translations, and example sentences
Add pronunciation notes when helpful
Use tags to organize by topic, level, situation, or anything that helps you find words later
Reuse vocabulary in exercises and review sessions
vocabulary.body: Instead of memorizing from a generic word list, you build a library that reflects your real learning journey.
vocabulary.exampleIntro: For example, you hear the Finnish word "varata" today:
vocabulary.exampleNote: That word is now part of your personal Notoria knowledge — ready for review and practice.
vocabulary.emphasis: Don't add every word you see. Add words that are meaningful to YOU.

theory.title: Theory
theory.intro: Theory is your personal language reference — a place to save knowledge you want to remember.
bullets: Grammar rules and patterns
Pronunciation notes
Usage explanations
Examples and personal notes
Things you repeatedly forget
theory.body: Write explanations in your own words. A grammar note doesn't have to sound like a textbook. If a simple explanation makes sense to you, that's a good explanation for your diary.
theory.emphasis: Theory is like a reference notebook you return to whenever you forget something.

exercise.title: Exercise
exercise.intro: Exercises let you actively practice the knowledge you've collected.
bullets: Flashcards
Quizzes and multiple choice
Fill-in-the-blank exercises
Vocabulary practice from your saved words
Grammar practice from your theory notes
Other formats based on your own material
exercise.emphasis: The value comes from practicing YOUR knowledge — not random vocabulary from a generic course, but the words and concepts you've personally decided are important.

writing.title: Writing
writing.intro: Writing is where passive knowledge becomes active language use.
bullets: Draft texts on topics you care about
Create question sets for yourself
Practice using vocabulary you've learned
Experiment with new grammar
Review and improve your writing over time
With Pro: use AI to check and improve your work
Export your writing when you need it
writing.emphasis: Your writing doesn't have to be perfect. The point is to use the language, make mistakes, notice what you don't know yet, and improve over time.

listening.title: Listening
listening.intro: Listening lets you study real content you choose — not just predefined lessons.
bullets: Upload audio or video
Generate a transcript
Study the transcript line by line
Turn the material into a lesson
Discover vocabulary and expressions from real content
listening.body: Bring something YOU actually want to understand into Notoria:
listening.emphasis: You control the content. Notoria helps you understand and learn from it.

speaking.title: Speaking
speaking.intro: Speaking is the active conversation part of your learning journey.
bullets: Talk with an AI tutor through video
Practice speaking naturally
Use vocabulary and knowledge you've collected
Review the conversation transcript afterward
Read feedback and identify areas to improve
speaking.emphasis: Speaking doesn't need to be perfect. The purpose is to practice using the language in a realistic situation — then learn from what happened.

inbox.title: Capture
inbox.intro: Capture is your quick drop zone — save something the moment you meet it, then decide later where it belongs.
bullets: Save a word, phrase, grammar doubt, or writing idea in seconds
Add an optional note or source for context
Keep items in To process until you are ready
Turn a capture into Vocabulary, Theory, Writing, or Exercise when you have time
An item is marked Processed only after you finish creating that linked entry
inbox.body: Capture sits at the start of the loop: collect first, organize second. You do not need a perfect category in the moment — you need the thought saved.
inbox.emphasis: If you only have ten seconds, capture is enough. Sorting can wait.
inbox.exampleIntro: For example, you overhear a phrase on the bus and only have a moment:
examples: Note: heard on the bus — booking an appointment
Later: process into Vocabulary with meaning and an example
inbox.exampleNote: The scrap is safe in Capture. When you have five quiet minutes, send it to Vocabulary (or Theory / Writing) and finish the entry — only then is it Processed.

connections.title: Your knowledge becomes your practice
connections.intro: Notoria becomes more useful as you keep adding things that matter to your learning:
paragraphs: Capture holds the scraps until you are ready to place them.
What you collect in Vocabulary and Theory becomes the source for your exercises.
Writing and Listening help you use and understand the language in new contexts.
Speaking puts it all into active conversation.
Review closes the loop — and each review often leads to new words and notes to add.
connections.highlight: The more knowledge you add that matters to you, the more useful and personal your practice becomes.

philosophy.title: This is your diary.
philosophy.lead: Notoria is a tool for your learning process — not a test of how well you are learning.
dontNeed: You don't need to make your notes perfect
You don't need to worry about whether your tags are "correct"
You don't need to write textbook-quality explanations
You don't need to finish every exercise
You don't need to use every feature
canDo: You can learn at your own pace.
philosophy.quote: Nobody is grading your diary. You're building it for yourself.

startHere.title: Getting started for the first time
startHere.intro: You don't need to set everything up before you begin. Just start with something you want to remember.

steps.language: Choose the language you want to learn.
steps.words: Add 5–10 words you actually want to remember.
steps.theory: Add one or two theory or grammar notes.
steps.exercise: Create an exercise from your knowledge.
steps.listeningSpeaking: When you're ready, try listening or speaking.
steps.return: Come back tomorrow and add something new.
steps.capture: Open Capture and save one quick note or phrase you want to come back to.

privacyPolicy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how Notoria (<site>www.notoria.fi</site>) handles personal data for its private language-learning web app. It is written to match how the product works today. If a practice is not described here, we do not claim to do it.

controller.title: 1. Who is responsible
controller.p1: Notoria is the language-learning service at <site>www.notoria.fi</site>, offered to users in Finland and the wider EU/EEA.
controller.p2: For privacy questions, data-subject requests, and other user contact, email <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact>.
controller.p3: A registered company name and postal address for the data controller are not published in the current product. If you need formal controller identification for a GDPR request, email <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact> and we will provide it.

scope.title: 2. What this policy covers
scope.p1: It covers personal data and learning content processed when you:
list: create or use an account
save material in private workspaces
subscribe to Notoria Pro
use optional AI-assisted tools
upload media for listening or profile use
use speaking practice
send feedback or contact us
scope.p2: The current application code does not include a third-party marketing analytics or advertising SDK. We do not claim to use trackers that are not present in the product.

data.title: 3. Data we process
data.p1: Notoria processes different kinds of data for different reasons. The main categories are:

accountAuth.title: Account and authentication
list: Name and email address
Password hash for email/password accounts (passwords are never stored in plain text)
Google account identifiers and OAuth tokens if you sign in with Google
Optional profile photo (avatar)
Account role and created/updated timestamps

learningContent.title: Learning content you create
learningContent.p1: Content you add in private workspaces, such as vocabulary, theory notes, writing documents, exercises and imported practice material, listening lessons (including media references and transcripts), speaking session transcripts and related session fields, folders, tags, and study progress such as flashcard reviews.
learningContent.p2: This is your learning material. Notoria stores it so you can return to it and practise from it.

subscription.title: Subscription and payment metadata
list: Plan (free or Pro) and subscription status
Stripe customer and subscription identifiers, and current period end when applicable
subscription.p1: Card numbers and payment-method secrets stay with Stripe. Notoria keeps only the billing metadata needed to reflect your Pro status.

device.title: Device and preference data
device.p1: Cookies and browser storage used for sign-in, locale, active workspace, AI assistance preferences, theme, and similar product settings. See <cookies>Cookies and device storage</cookies>.

support.title: Support and feedback
support.list1: In-app feedback from Support (message, feedback type, your email, whether you are signed in, optional account id, page path, user-agent, and up to three optional image attachments)
support.p1: Feedback is delivered by email to Notoria’s technical inbox (<technical></technical>). It is not stored as a separate ticket database inside Notoria.

purposes.title: 4. Why we process data

rows.purpose: Provide accounts, workspaces, and your saved learning material
Authenticate you (email/password or Google) and reset passwords
Run Notoria Pro billing and subscription status via Stripe
Optional AI help, listening transcription, and speaking practice when you use those features
Keep the service secure and reliable (abuse prevention, debugging)
Respond to support and feedback messages
rows.basis: Legitimate interests / contract, depending on the request

purposes.p1: If you need a formal legal-basis note for a specific activity, email <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact>.

auth.title: 5. Accounts and sign-in
auth.p1: Notoria uses Auth.js (NextAuth) with a JWT session. You can sign in with email and password, or with Google OAuth when Google sign-in is configured.
auth.p2: Password-reset emails are sent only for accounts that have a password. Reset tokens are stored hashed, expire after 30 minutes, and are used only to set a new password.

ai.title: 6. AI features
ai.p1: Optional AI features in the current product use OpenAI. Depending on the tool you use, Notoria may send relevant learning content — for example vocabulary items, writing text or selections, exercise or theory context, listening transcripts, speaking transcripts, or live audio for the speaking tutor.
ai.p2: AI assistance preferences (including whether assistance is enabled) are stored in a browser cookie so the product can respect your settings. Many server actions that call the model check that assistance is enabled first. Turning assistance off in <settings>Settings</settings> blocks AI tools that require it.
ai.p3: Listening transcription via AssemblyAI can still run when you use Listening features that need a transcript, because transcription is part of that media workflow rather than the optional “AI assistance” preference alone.
ai.p4: The current codebase does not use other large-language-model providers besides OpenAI. OpenAI processes data under its own terms and privacy policy as a processor for these features.

payments.title: 7. Payments (Notoria Pro)
payments.p1: Paid subscriptions are handled by Stripe. Checkout, invoices, payment methods, and cancellation run through Stripe Checkout and the Stripe Customer Portal. Stripe webhooks update your plan and status in Notoria.
payments.p2: Stripe processes payment data as a payment provider. See Stripe’s own privacy documentation for card handling.

processors.title: 8. Service providers
processors.p1: Depending on which features you use, personal data or learning content may be processed by:

rows.role: Application hosting (configured region includes Frankfurt / fra1)
Avatars, listening media, editor images, and exercise-import files
Live speaking calls; automatic transcription; session fields such as transcript URLs (and recording URLs only if a recording event is later received)
Optional AI assistance and speaking-tutor realtime audio
Password-reset email and Support feedback delivery
Notoria Pro checkout, portal, and subscription status
OAuth sign-in when you choose Google; web fonts for the UI
Generated avatar images used in speaking sessions (from a name seed; no account password is sent)

processors.p2: Speaking calls are created with transcription enabled. Recording is disabled at call creation in the current implementation; a recording URL is stored only if the product later receives a recording-ready event from Stream.

cookies.title: 9. Cookies and device storage
cookies.p1: Notoria uses cookies and similar storage for necessary product functions. There is no separate Cookie Policy because the current implementation does not include advertising or analytics cookie programmes that would require one.

rows.purpose: Keeps you signed in (JWT session; library default naming)

cookies.p2: Your browser may also store theme preference (via next-themes), onboarding/tutorial flags, keyboard and motion preferences, view-mode choices, temporary exercise or flashcard session state, and similar client-only settings.
cookies.p3: Clearing local preferences in Settings removes those device preferences. It does not delete your account or workspace content on the server.

transfers.title: 10. International transfers
transfers.p1: Some providers above are based outside the EEA (for example in the United States) or may process data in more than one region. Where personal data leaves the EEA/UK, transfers rely on the safeguards those providers offer under applicable law — such as Standard Contractual Clauses where they apply — and on their published privacy terms.
transfers.p2: Application hosting for Notoria is configured toward the Frankfurt region (fra1). Ask <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact> if you need help finding the relevant provider documentation for a specific feature.

retention.title: 11. How long we keep data
list: Account and learning data are kept while your account remains open so you can use the service
Password-reset tokens expire after 30 minutes
Subscription metadata is kept as needed to reflect your current Pro status and Stripe billing relationship
Support and feedback emails are retained as long as needed to handle your request and related follow-up
retention.p1: Exact backup retention windows for infrastructure providers are not hard-coded in the application and may follow those providers’ operational practices. Contact us if you need clarification for a deletion request.

deletion.title: 12. Export and account deletion
deletion.exportP1: From <account>Account</account> you can download a JSON backup of workspaces and learning content (including vocabulary, theory notes, exercises/writing, listening lessons, and speaking sessions). Media files are referenced by URL rather than embedded as binary files.
deletion.exportP2: The current export does not include every account-related record. For example, flashcard progress/reviews and exercise-import source records are not part of the JSON backup. OAuth tokens, password hashes, and Stripe identifiers are not exported.
deletion.deleteP1: You can permanently delete your account from <account>Account</account>. When deletion succeeds, Notoria:
deleteList: deletes your user record and cascaded learning data from Notoria’s database
cancels and removes related Stripe customer data where Stripe is configured (best effort)
destroys avatar media and listening-lesson media that the deletion flow is implemented to remove from Cloudinary
deletion.deleteP2: The current deletion flow does not claim to purge every third-party artefact automatically. In particular, some Cloudinary assets (such as editor images or exercise-import files) and Stream speaking-call artefacts may remain subject to those providers until cleaned up separately or purged under their own schedules.
deletion.deleteP3: After deletion, limited residual copies may also remain briefly in encrypted backups or logs until those systems rotate. If something specific remains after you delete your account, email <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact>.

rights.title: 13. Your rights (GDPR)
rights.p1: If you are in the EU/EEA or otherwise protected by GDPR, you may have the right to:

correct inaccurate data
erase data (including by deleting your account)
restrict or object to certain processing
receive a portable copy of data you provided (see Export above)
withdraw consent where processing is based on consent
rights.listComplaint: lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority — in Finland, the Office of the Data Protection Ombudsman (<ombudsman>tietosuoja.fi</ombudsman>)
rights.p2: To exercise these rights, email <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact>. We may need to verify that the request comes from the account holder.

children.title: 14. Children
children.p1: Notoria requires an account and is built as a personal learning workspace. The product does not implement a dedicated age-gate. It is not directed at children. If you believe a child’s data has been submitted without appropriate authority, contact <contact>contact@notoria.fi</contact>.

changes.p2: When a change is material, we will communicate it in a reasonable way available at the time — for example by updating this page and, where appropriate, an in-product notice or email.

about.title: About Notoria
about.lede: A private workspace for self-studying any language — built around the material you bring in, not a catalogue you scroll through.

what.title: What it is
what.p1: Notoria is a private workspace for self-studying a language. You keep vocabulary, notes, theory, exercises, writing, listening, and speaking in one place, organised by the language you are learning.
what.p2: It is not a school platform and not a library of ready-made courses. It is a home for the material you collect and create yourself — the words worth keeping, the explanations that finally stick, the practice that belongs to your actual progress.
what.beat: Your material. Your language. One place.

why.title: Why Notoria
why.p1: Language learning gets more useful when the pieces stay connected.
why.p2: A word you saved last week should be easy to practise again. A note you wrote in your own words should still be there when the same pattern confuses you. Writing, listening, and speaking should be able to draw on that same material — instead of living in separate corners of your phone and desktop.
why.p3: Notoria keeps those threads together, so practice feels continuous rather than scattered.

who.title: Who it is for
who.p1: People who learn independently — and want their own material to stay at the centre of the process.
who.p2: If you prefer collecting what matters to you over following someone else’s fixed syllabus, Notoria is meant for that rhythm. Calm enough for serious study. Practical enough for everyday return visits.

yourWay.title: Your material, your way
yourWay.p1: Books, teachers, courses, podcasts, conversations, and everything else you already use still matter. Notoria does not try to replace them.
yourWay.p2: What it offers instead is a place to bring those materials together: save what you notice, organise it by language, explain it in your own words, and keep practising from it.
yourWay.beat: Notoria sits beside your learning life. It does not try to become it.

provides.title: What you can do
provides.intro: Inside a workspace, the main pieces fit together:

items.vocab: Build a personal vocabulary bank with meanings, examples, and tags
items.practice: Practise with exercises drawn from your own words and notes
items.create: Write theory notes and writing work you can revisit later
items.listenSpeak: Turn media into listening practice, and speak with an AI tutor on Pro

provides.note: Some AI, listening, speaking, and export tools are part of Notoria Pro. The free plan still covers everyday vocabulary practice and the core study loop.

ai.title: AI, where it helps
ai.p1: When AI is available, it is a supporting tool — not the centre of the product.
ai.p2: It can help shape practice, check writing, or support listening and speaking. It does not decide what you should learn, and it does not replace the work of noticing, remembering, and returning.
ai.p3: You stay in charge of what enters the workspace and what you come back to.

ourStory.title: Our story
ourStory.lede: Language-learning tools were everywhere. The material that actually mattered was still nowhere when it was time to practise.

frustration.title: The familiar scatter
frustration.p1: If you have ever tried to learn a language seriously on your own, you know the shape of it.
frustration.p2: Words live in one app. Grammar notes in a document. Examples screenshotted into a folder you stop opening. Listening on a phone. Writing somewhere else. Speaking almost never connected to any of it.
frustration.p3: You can collect a lot. That part is easy.
frustration.p4: The hard part arrives later — when you sit down to practise and realise nothing shares a place. Each tool remembers a fragment. None of them remember the language you are actually building.
frustration.beat: Useful material, scattered. Practice, starting over.

realisation.title: The thing that should have been obvious
realisation.p1: At some point the frustration stops being about more features and becomes about the centre of gravity.
realisation.p2: The learner’s own material — the words worth keeping, the notes written in their own words, the examples that finally made something click — should not sit outside the tools used to practise. It should be the loop.
realisation.p3: Practice that ignores what you have already gathered is just busywork with better branding.
realisation.beat: Your material belongs at the centre.

exists.title: Why Notoria exists
exists.p1: Notoria exists to give that material a private home — and to keep vocabulary, notes, theory, exercises, writing, listening, and speaking inside one workspace built around it.
exists.p2: Not as a pile of disconnected modules with a shared login. As a place where what you save can become what you practise, and what you practise can deepen what you keep.
exists.p3: You bring the language in. Notoria helps you stay with it — revisit it, drill it, write with it, hear it, speak it — without losing the thread every time you switch tools.
exists.p4: That is the whole idea, stated plainly.

believes.title: What we believe
believes.p1: Self-study should feel personal, practical, and connected. Not performative. Not endlessly interrupted by catalogues of content you did not ask for.
believes.p2: Notoria is not a school. It is not a course marketplace. It is not trying to replace teachers, textbooks, or the quiet work of paying attention.
believes.p3: It is a workspace for the language you are learning — private enough to be yours, structured enough to be useful, light enough that the product stays out of the way of the learning.

going.title: Where it is going
going.p1: The direction is not dramatic. Stay private. Stay practical. Stay honest about what software can and cannot do.
going.p2: Keep improving the learning loop around your own material — the connections between remembering, understanding, producing, listening, and speaking.
going.p3: Use AI where it genuinely helps: shaping practice, supporting writing, listening, or speaking. Not as a gimmick. Not as a substitute for the learner’s own work. Not as an excuse to fill the product with noise.
going.closing: Notoria was built because someone got tired of the disconnect — and wanted a better place for their own learning material. That reason still holds.

howToUse.title: How to use Notoria
howToUse.lede: A practical map of the learning loop — start with a few words, then grow practice, writing, listening, and speaking when you are ready.

intro.title: A workspace, not a course
intro.p1: Notoria is a private place for the language you are already learning. You bring material in, keep it organised, and practise from it — instead of starting from a catalogue of lessons you did not choose.
intro.p2: Each workspace is one language. Capture, Vocabulary, Theory, exercises, writing, listening, and speaking live together there, so what you save can become what you practise.
intro.beat: You do not need to learn Notoria all at once. You grow it with the language.

loop.title: The learning loop
loop.p1: Most of the product sits on one simple loop:

bring.label: Bring in
bring.body: Save words, phrases, and notes — use Capture for fast scraps, or add straight into Vocabulary and Theory from lessons, books, media, and conversations.

organise.label: Organise
organise.body: Keep everything for that language in one workspace, with meanings, examples, and tags that help you find things again.

understand.label: Understand
understand.body: Write theory notes in your own words when a pattern needs explaining — grammar, usage, or something you keep forgetting.

practise.label: Practise
practise.body: Turn what you have saved into exercises and review, so memory work comes from your own material.

use.label: Use
use.body: Write with it, listen to it, and speak it — so the language moves beyond recognition into active use.

review.label: Come back
review.body: Return later, add what is new, revisit what was hard, and keep the loop going instead of starting over.

loop.beat: Bring in → organise → understand → practise → use → come back.

startSmall.title: Start small
startSmall.p1: Notoria is not something you complete. There is no checklist that means you are done with the product.
startSmall.p2: A good first day can be a workspace, a couple of Capture notes, and five words you actually care about. Notes, longer practice, writing, listening, and speaking can wait until they earn a place in your loop.

firstSession.title: A first session
firstSession.intro: If you want a concrete starting path, try this once:

workspace.title: Create a workspace
workspace.body: Make one for the language you are learning, and give it a name you will recognise later.

words.title: Add a handful of words
words.body: Open Vocabulary and save words or phrases you want to remember, with meanings or examples if they help. Or drop a quick scrap in Capture first and process it later.

notes.title: Write a short note if you need one
notes.body: In Theory, capture a grammar or usage point in your own words — only when something needs explaining.

practice.title: Do a short practice
practice.body: Open Exercise and practise from the material you just added — flashcards or drills built from your own words.

return.title: Come back tomorrow
return.body: Add a little more, revisit a note, or practise again. Continuity matters more than covering every area on day one.

connect.title: How the areas connect
connect.p1: Capture is the quick entry point. Vocabulary and Theory are where material settles. Exercise turns that material into practice. Writing, Listening, and Speaking help you use the language more actively.
connect.p2: You do not have to move through every area in order. Many people stay with words and short practice for a while.
connect.p3: A natural next step is writing when you want to produce language on your own terms, then listening and speaking when you want the same material to work in your ear and voice — Listening and Speaking are part of Notoria Pro.
connect.beat: Collect and understand first. Use and speak when the material is ready to leave the page.

areas.title: The main areas
areas.intro: A short map of what each area is for:

vocab.label: Vocabulary
vocab.body: Your personal word bank — meanings, examples, tags, and flashcard progress. This is usually the foundation everything else draws from.

theory.label: Theory
theory.body: Grammar and usage notes written in your own words, ready to revisit when the same pattern shows up again.

exercises.label: Exercise
exercises.body: Practice sessions from your vocabulary, theory notes, or imported material — so drills stay tied to what you have actually saved.

writing.label: Writing
writing.body: Documents and question sets for using the language actively, not only recognising it.

listening.label: Listening
listening.body: Turn media into listening practice in your workspace. Available on Notoria Pro.

speaking.label: Speaking
speaking.body: Live practice with an AI tutor, grounded in the language you are studying. Available on Notoria Pro.

capture.label: Capture
capture.body: A fast drop zone for scraps — words, doubts, and ideas — that you process into Vocabulary, Theory, Writing, or Exercise later. Capture first when you only have a moment; items stay unprocessed until you finish creating the linked entry.

notEverything.title: You do not need to use everything
notEverything.p1: Skip areas that do not help right now. A quiet vocabulary bank and a few notes can already be a strong system.
notEverything.p2: Add Exercise when you want structured review. Add Writing when you want to produce. Add Listening and Speaking when hearing and saying the language is the next useful step.

cta.title: Ready to start?

support.title: Support
support.lede: Quick answers to common questions, and a simple way to send feedback when you need to.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.lede: Start here — most answers take less than a minute to read.

workspace.q: What is a workspace, and how do I switch languages?
workspace.a: Each workspace is one language you are learning. Vocabulary, theory, writing, exercises, listening, and speaking stay inside that workspace. Create or switch workspaces from the workspace menu in the app.

start.a: Create a workspace for the language you are learning, add a few words in <vocabulary>Vocabulary</vocabulary>, then try a short exercise. For the learning approach, see <howToUse>How to Use</howToUse>. Signed in? Open the in-app <gettingStarted>Getting started</gettingStarted> guide for a UI walkthrough.

account.q: How do I change my password or close my account?
account.a: Open <account>Account</account>. You can update your password there if you use email sign-in, manage Notoria Pro, export a backup, or permanently delete your account.

pro.q: How do billing and cancellation work?
pro.a: Notoria Pro is billed through Stripe. From <account>Account</account> you can upgrade, open the Stripe customer portal to manage payment methods and invoices, or cancel renewal.

proFeatures.q: What is free, and what needs Notoria Pro?
proFeatures.a: Everyday vocabulary practice and related study tools are available on the free plan. Some AI tools, listening, speaking, and document export features are part of Notoria Pro. Compare and upgrade from <account>Account</account>.

learning.q: How do Notoria’s learning features work?
learning.a: Notoria keeps vocabulary, theory, exercises, writing, listening, and speaking in one workspace so practice can use material you saved. Start with words and notes, then add practice and active use when you are ready. <about>About</about> explains the product; <howToUse>How to Use</howToUse> maps the learning loop.

ai.q: Can I turn AI help off?
ai.a: Yes. AI assistance preferences are in <settings>Settings</settings>. When assistance is off, AI tools that require it stay blocked.

data.q: Where is my learning content stored?
data.a: Your account and learning data live in Notoria’s database. Media such as avatars and listening files is stored with our media host. See the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> for processors and deletion details.

backup.q: Can I export or back up my data?
backup.a: Yes. From <account>Account</account> you can download a JSON backup of your workspaces and learning content. Media files are linked by URL, not embedded. For privacy and deletion details, see the <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy>.
